description: Five CS students uniting strong software engineering, machine learning, and rapid prototyping skills to turn complex NASA Earth and space data into practical, accessible tools for real-world impact.
summary:
TrendScope — Earth System Trend Detective investigates 24 years of vegetation change in Egypt's Nile Delta (2001–2024, 288 months) using NASA MODIS MOD13A3.061 NDVI data. Because seasonal vegetation
  │ swings hide long-term environmental shifts, TrendScope removes seasonal cycles to compute monthly NDVI anomalies, Sen's slope (-0.02131 NDVI/decade), and Mann–Kendall trend significance (tau = -0.341, p
  │ = 5.727e-18). Built with a deterministic Python pipeline and an interactive React/TypeScript web explorer, it helps researchers, agronomists, and decision-makers distinguish real long-term vegetation
  │ decline from seasonal noise.
details:
TrendScope pairs a deterministic Python 3.12 data and statistics pipeline (numpy, scipy, pandas, pytest, ruff) with an interactive React/TypeScript/Vite web explorer deployed on Vercel. Working

features:

│ real observed 288-month Nile Delta NDVI baseline (2001-01 to 2024-12, is_mock=false, 100% coverage), interactive 2D Map & 3D Globe locator, Anomaly vs. Raw Value time-series chart with Sen's slope

│ trendline, and a Scientific Verdict card that transparently displays statistical caveats (verified by 226 Python tests, 20 frontend tests, and 50 Playwright Chromium E2E tests in CI). Limitations: live

│ arbitrary-AOI NASA raster processing is disabled in public static hosting because it requires a dedicated backend with Earthdata credentials, and the primary Mann–Kendall test is uncorrected for serial

│ autocorrelation (explicitly labeled in the UI). Future plans: deploy a hosted worker backend for custom regions and add Hamed–Rao autocorrelation correction
